Open Start and type your company name and your limits in the yellow cells: statement and payment days, tax due day, co-host fee percent, lowest net to owner and the reserve to hold.
Check Owners, Units, Cities, Team and Fee Tiers. They hold the people, the units, the local tax percent of each city and the fee percent of each package; the other sheets look them up.

At the end of each month fill Owner Statements: revenue, platform fees, cleaning, supplies, maintenance, utilities and the management percent. The management fee, the net to owner, the margin and the checks calculate themselves.
Add the lines behind each statement on Statement Lines, one per unit and kind, with the booking or repair it comes from. Revenue, net and fee per unit fill in on Units.
Record each payment to an owner on Owner Payments with its method. A statement paid in two parts has two rows; the payment check shows what is on time, late or delayed.
Keep Bookings, Expenses, Cleaner Pay and Maintenance Costs up to date so every statement can be checked against its source.
On Co-host Fees enter the month, the net revenue and the messages answered; the fee and the fee per message calculate themselves. Log the work on Co-host Duties.
On Local Tax enter nights, room revenue, the tax collected, what the host collected and what the platforms reported. You see what to remit, the due date and any difference.
Write each correction on Tax Adjustments with its reason and filing date. The tax to remit on Local Tax includes the adjustments.
Track repair reserves on Owner Reserves, owner requests on Owner Requests, owner stays on Owner Stays and the term, notice date and renewal of each contract on Owner Contracts.
Use the 14 calculators for statements, fees, payment dates, the reserve, local tax, the tax calendar and check, owner stays, fee tiers, owner return and a percent grid.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in. Check your own local rules for tax forms and dates.
Read the Owner and Tax Dashboard and the Charts every month: revenue, net to owner, fees, costs, statements, co-host fees, local tax, requests and reserves.

extra units, rate changes, occupancy and cost changes show the extra yearly profit of each plan from your own last 12 months

Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: wanted occupancy and margin, cash floor, owner draw, tax set-aside share and the longest payback you accept for a new unit.
Check Units, Break-Even Rows and Team. They hold your units, their fixed costs and the people the other sheets look up.
Fill Unit Profit by Month: one row for each unit and month with revenue and each cost. Total costs, profit, margin, profit per night and occupancy calculate themselves.
Log bookings on Bookings and each payout on Payouts. Late, short and missing payouts turn red with the amount still missing.
Enter every cost on Expenses, Cleaner Pay, Supply Purchases and Maintenance Costs. Rent and bills sit in Unit Profit by Month.
Keep Cash Months up to date at the end of each month. It gives closing cash, months of cover, the floor check and the safe owner draw. Owner Draws records what you took.
Update Cash Forecast every week with the payouts you expect and the costs you must pay. It shows the balance of each of the next 13 weeks against your cash floor.
Record owner statements, co-host fees and local occupancy tax (a tax on each night, collected from the guest) on their own sheets. The amount left to remit is flagged.
Use Income Tax Set-Aside to hold back your share of profit each month and see the balance. Check your own local rules and ask your accountant for the amount due.
List your leases and loans on Loans and Leases. A lease that ends within the warning days turns amber.
Plan growth on Unit Pipeline and Growth Scenarios: set-up cost, rent, rate and occupancy give the yearly profit and payback; each scenario shows the extra yearly profit.
Use the 14 calculators for profit, break-even, cash, the safe draw, tax set-aside, payout gaps, a new unit, keep or drop, rate rises and direct bookings.
Read the Profit and Cash Dashboard and Charts every month: revenue, profit, margin, cash, break-even and growth.
